questions.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}=\frac{2x+B}{{x}^{2}+20}-\frac{1}{x+1},
$$

where $B$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $B.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-5x-27 & =(2x+B)(x+1)-({x}^{2}+20).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}-5(0)-27 & =(2(0)+B)(0+1)-({0}^{2}+20) \\ -27 & =B-20 \\ B & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x-7}{{x}^{2}+20}-\frac{1}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x-7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+20=u.$ Then, $2x\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+20).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+20}\,\text{d}x & =7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+(2\sqrt{5})^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =7\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2\sqrt{5}}) \\  & =\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{10}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{10}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}-5x-27}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+20)}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+20)-\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{10}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{10})-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}+20}{(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)}=\frac{x-2}{{x}^{2}+8}+\frac{D}{x+2},
$$

where $D$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{4{x}^{2}+20}{(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)}\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $D.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}+20 & =(x-2)(x+2)+D({x}^{2}+8).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)^{2}+20 & =(0-2)(0+2)+D({0}^{2}+8) \\ 20 & =-4+8D \\ 24 & =8D \\ D & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}+20}{(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{x-2}{{x}^{2}+8}+\frac{3}{x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+8=u.$ Then, $x\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+8).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}2\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+8}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+(2\sqrt{2})^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2\sqrt{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}x}{4}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we get

$$
3\int \frac{1}{x+2}\text{d}x=3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}+20}{(x+2)({x}^{2}+8)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+8)-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}x}{4})+3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+C\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}=\frac{Ax+1}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{1}{x-1},
$$

where $A$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $A.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+x+3 & =(Ax+1)(x-1)+{x}^{2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=2$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{2}+2+3 & =(A(2)+1)(2-1)+{2}^{2}+4 \\ 9 & =2A+1+8 \\ 9 & =2A+9 \\ A & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{0x+1}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{1}{x-1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}=\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{D}{x+2},
$$

where $D$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $D.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+4x+3 & =2x(x+2)+D({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=-2$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-2)^{2}+4(-2)+3 & =2(-2)(-2+2)+D((-2)^{2}+3) \\ 7 & =7D \\ D & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{1}{x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+3=u.$ Then, $2x\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+3| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+4x+3}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3)+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|+C\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}=\frac{2x+B}{{x}^{2}+5}-\frac{1}{x+1},
$$

where $B$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $B.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+5x-2 & =(2x+B)(x+1)-({x}^{2}+5).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{0}^{2}+5(0)-2 & =(2(0)+B)(0+1)-({0}^{2}+5) \\ -2 & =B-5 \\ B & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x+3}{{x}^{2}+5}-\frac{1}{x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{3}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution ${x}^{2}+5=u.$ Then, $2x\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+5).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+5}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+(\sqrt{5})^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{5}}) \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{5}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we get

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+1}\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x-2}{(x+1)({x}^{2}+5)}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+5)+\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}x}{5})-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+6$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+6}+\frac{C}{x-3}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+6)(x-3),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}-7x & =(Ax+B)(x-3)+C({x}^{2}+6).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=-4,$ and $C=-2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)} & =\frac{x-4}{{x}^{2}+6}-\frac{2}{x-3}\end{aligned}
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{x-4}{{x}^{2}+6}-\frac{2}{x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-4\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+6.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{u}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+6| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+6).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{6}}).
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{-{x}^{2}-7x}{({x}^{2}+6)(x-3)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-4\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+6}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+6)-\frac{4}{\sqrt{6}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{6}})-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+K\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{C}{x+4}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $({x}^{2}+3)(x+4),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+5x-9 & =(Ax+B)(x+4)+C({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=2,B=-3,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)} & =\frac{2x-3}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{1}{x+4}\end{aligned}
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x-3}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{1}{x+4})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+3.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+3| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x & =3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}x}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+4|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+5x-9}{({x}^{2}+3)(x+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x+4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+3)-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}x}{3})+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+4|+K\end{aligned}
$$

\frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}=\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+9}+\frac{C}{x-3}

$$
{x}^{2}+x+42=(Ax+B)(x-3)+C({x}^{2}+9).
$$

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+x+42}{({x}^{2}+9)(x-3)}=-\frac{2x+5}{{x}^{2}+9}+\frac{3}{x-3}.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+9}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+9| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+9).\end{aligned}

questions.worked_solution:
The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+1$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+1}.
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-1)({x}^{2}+1),$ and we get

$$
2=A({x}^{2}+1)+(Bx+C)(x-1).
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=-1,$ and $C=-1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}=\frac{1}{x-1}+\frac{-x-1}{{x}^{2}+1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x-1}+\frac{-x-1}{{x}^{2}+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+1.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+1| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$

$$

The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+4$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+4x+12}{(x-2)({x}^{2}+4)}=\frac{A}{x-2}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+4}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-2)({x}^{2}+4),$ and we get

$$
{x}^{2}+4x+12=A({x}^{2}+4)+(Bx+C)(x-2).
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=3,B=-2,$ and $C=0.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+4x+12}{(x-2)({x}^{2}+4)} & =\frac{3}{x-2}+\frac{-2x+0}{{x}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{3}{x-2}-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+4x+12}{(x-2)({x}^{2}+4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{3}{x-2}-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4})\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|.
$$

             

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+4.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+4x+12}{(x-2)({x}^{2}+4)}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4)+K\end{aligned}
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+9x-4}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1)}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1),$ and we get

$$

$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=2,B=1$ and $C=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+9x-4}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1)}=\frac{2}{x-1}+\frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3{x}^{2}+9x-4}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+4x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x-1}+\frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
2\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x=2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}+4x-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4x-1|.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{15-25x}{(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)(x-4)}\,\text{d}x & =5\int \frac{2x-3}{2{x}^{2}-6x+9}\,\text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{2}-6x+9))-5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|+K \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{2}-6x+9)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|+K\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.problem:
Given that 

$$
\dfrac{4x^2-6}{(x-3)(x^2+1)} = \dfrac{A}{x-3} + \dfrac{x+3}{x^2 + 1},
$$

where $A$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\displaystyle{\int \dfrac{4x^2-6}{(x-3)(x^2+1)}\,\textrm d x}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the constant $A.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-3)(x^2 + 1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-6=A({x}^{2}+1)+{x}^{2}-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)^{2}-6 & =A({0}^{2}+1)+{0}^{2}-9 \\ -6 & =A-9 \\ A & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\eqalign{
\int \dfrac{4x^2 - 6}{(x-3)(x^2+1)} \, \textrm{d}x & = \int \left(\dfrac{3}{x-3} + \dfrac{x+3}{x^2 + 1}\right) \textrm{d}x \[5pt]

& = 3\int\dfrac{1}{x-3}\,\textrm{d}x + \int \dfrac{x}{x^2+1}\,\textrm d x + 3\int \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 1} \, \textrm{d}x
	}
$$

For the first integral, we get

$$
\int \dfrac{1}{x-3} \textrm{d}x = \ln|x-3|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $x^2 + 1 = u.$ Then, $2x\,\textrm{d}x=\textrm{d}u,$ and we get 

$$
\eqalign{
\int \dfrac{x}{x^2+1}\,\textrm{d}x & = \int \left(\dfrac{1}{u}\right) \dfrac{\textrm d u}{2} \[5pt]

&= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \vert u\vert \[5pt]

&= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \vert x^2 + 1\vert \[5pt]

& = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left(x^2+1\right).							
}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we use the fact that $\displaystyle \int \dfrac{1}{x^2 + a^2} \, \textrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right),$ which results in

$$
\int \dfrac{1}{x^2+1}\,\textrm{d}x = \arctan{x}.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-6}{(x-3)({x}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+3\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$
